messages:
anya: heads up — seeing a bunch of requests come back with no upstream span after the gateway republished into the async queue.
anya: reproduction: http://logs/infra/req123 — gateway receives request with traceparent, calls out, then republishes to SQS for async work, worker shows a fresh root span instead of linking.
sam: yup saw that yesterday. my hunch is the republish path strips headers and we rely on message attributes which our lambda wrapper normalizes incorrectly.
miguel: we already use message attributes for `traceparent` in some flow, but SQS FIFO + dlq + delay retries means attributes can get dropped on republish by some of our helper libs.
nora: quick question — are we losing full span payloads or just the trace context? i.e., do we still get parent ids or no trace at all?
anya: only trace context (trace-id, parent-id, sampled) — so workers create new root spans. that breaks UI stitching for long-running pipelines.
sam: two surface fixes: 1) ensure gateway injects minimal carrier into message attributes (traceparent or our compact `rw-tp`) and test libs preserve them on republish; 2) introduce a tiny span-bridge store (redis with TTL) where gateway writes a minimal span handle and attribute points to it — worker can rehydrate the trace from the handle.
miguel: +1 for the handle store for multi-hop stuff. downside: cross-tenant isolation + retention + perf. if we use redis in each region we need TTL of maybe 1h and a small serialized carrier (span-context + sampling + optional tags).
nora: concerned about PII & logs — storing any baggage in the bridge is risky. we should only store the absolute minimum: trace-id, parent-id, sampled, orig-service. no user-level baggage.
anya: agreed. suggest schema: `rw-span-handle:v1` -> base64(JSON{"trace_id", "parent_id", "flags", "src"}). store key is uuid, put key in message attribute `rw-span-handle`.
sam: worker flow: on message receive, if `traceparent` exists prefer it. else if `rw-span-handle` present, call span-bridge internal endpoint `GET /v1/rehydrate/:id` with short-lived cert (mTLS) to fetch context and then start a span with remote parent.
miguel: what about retries where the worker republishes again? we need to propagate `rw-span-handle` when we republish or extend TTL on bridge read.
nora: extend TTL on bridge read seems fine but be careful about thundering herd on retries. maybe increment a small `retry_count` in handle and reject after N.
anya: performance note — bridge should be in-path but tiny (single-digit ms) and cached by workers locally for hot ids to avoid extra hop for common patterns.
sam: edge-case: if bridge unavailable, fallback to creating new root but add attribute `rw-link-to-original:<id>` so UI can attempt best-effort join via async job later.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: canary deploy of `gateway-republish-preserve-attrs` started at 2026-03-19T09:14Z on prod-us-east-1 (ci/1234)
miguel: plan for rollout: feature flag in gateway + workers. ramp 10% traffic for 24h, run sampling to ensure spans stitch correctly, then flip for 100%.
nora: add an eval in console: timeline view should show a dashed link when worker rehydrated via handle vs direct parent — makes it obvious which traces crossed async boundary.
anya: I'll draft a short design doc with sequence diagrams and security considerations (no baggage, TTL, auth) and open a PR for the bridge service.
sam: I'll add tests to our sqs helper libs to ensure attributes survive republish paths (incl lambdas, consumer republish helpers).
miguel: also add a small loadtest for bridge at 5000 rps to see latency tail.
nora: tagging infra to review redis clusters and keys-per-second cost.
anya: thanks team — next step: doc + PRs. cc @sam @miguel @nora
